preamble: Diphthongization of the near-open front vowel [æ] to the opening diphthong [ie]. In Samic, the Proto-Uralic first-syllable *ä gave Proto-Samic *ie when the second syllable had *ë (from earlier *i): *käte 'hand' > *kietë > Northern Sami giehta, against Finnish käsi; before second-syllable *ä it gave *ā instead. In Slovak, Proto-Slavic yat *ě, reconstructed as [æː ~ eː], appears as the diphthong ie /i̯ɛ/ (biely 'white', viera 'faith'), where Russian has e and Polish ia or e.

examples.to: Proto-Samic *kietë > Northern Sami giehta, South Sami gïete
examples.note: Conditioned by second-syllable *ë; Finnish käsi keeps ä. Wikipedia reconstructs internal steps *ǟ > *ē > *ie with no attested intermediate.

examples.to: Proto-Samic *kielë > Northern Sami giella, South Sami gïele
Proto-Samic *liemë > Northern Sami liepma, South Sami lïeme
Proto-Samic *mielkë > Northern Sami mielga, South Sami mïelke
examples.note: Before second-syllable *ä the same vowel gives *ā instead (*äjmä > *ājmē).
